html:
Bridgetown, the capital of Barbados, was founded by English settlers in 1628 by a bridge over the Constitution River. It grew into one of the busiest ports of the English Americas.

Sugar, rum and molasses went out from its wharves, and enslaved Africans came in. Its garrison, built up in the 1700s, was a main British base in the region. The young George Washington visited in 1751, his only trip abroad.

Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011. The city remains the island's centre, home to its parliament, one of the oldest in the Americas, and to Codrington College nearby, all within the story of English Barbados.
